episodes.165573: Widespread rain ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley resulted in some localized flooding.
episodes.165677: A low pressure system emerging from the Tennessee Valley tracked into West Virginia on the evening of February 24th, spreading periods of rain into the state. Over an inch of rain fell that evening and resulted in flooded roadways in the towns of Dunbar, Gandeeville, and Spencer. Even after the rain had ended days prior, water flowing down from northern West Virginia and southwest Pennsylvania resulted in a rise along the Ohio River. The gage at Point Pleasant observed this rise occurring on the 26th and would remain in flood for the next two days, resulting in many roadways and homes located within Point Pleasant to observe high water issues.
episodes.165693: A wave of low pressure tracking close to the area on February 24th brought rain showers into southeast Ohio and northward. While the disturbance and its coinciding cold front departed the area on the 25th, flooding did not begin to take place until later that afternoon as local creeks and streams poured into the mainstem rivers. River and stream gages along Duck Creek, the Little Muskingum River, and the Muskingum River noted these rises and did not observe a return to their banks until the early morning hours of the 26th. This mainly resulted in minor flooding of nearby fields as well as roads located close by to the gage.
episodes.166283: Heavy rain brought flooding to the White River in late February.
episodes.167134: A slow moving low pressure system across the Great Lakes brought unseasonable heavy rainfall to the region on February 25th, one to one and half inches of rainfall was reported in some areas.

events.narrative: High water was observed on the southbound side of Roxalana Road at Lower Midway Drive in Dunbar.

High water and debris flowed along Route 119 between Walton and Gandeeville which resulted in road closures in several spots. Spring Creek rose out of its banks and spilled onto Front Street in the town of Spencer. Johnson Creek Road observed high water as the nearby creek rose out of its banks.
High water was reported at the intersection of Blue Creek and Cassel Run Roads.
Heavy rain caused several farms adjacent to Armbrust Brinkerton Road to flood.

In the early afternoon hours of February 25th, the West Fork of Duck Creek rose out of its 13 foot bankfull level, cresting at 13.55 feet just after midnight on the 26th, and returned to its banks a few hours later. Backwater from the creek resulted in minor flooding of nearby fields and campgrounds.

In Bloomfield, the Little Muskingum River rose out of its 16 foot bankfull level on the afternoon of February 25th. The river crested at 18.84 feet that evening then returned to its banks very early on the 26th. While out of its banks, the river spilled onto State Route 260 where it intersects with Route 26.
Heavy rain brought flooding to the White River at Clarendon in late February.

The Muskingum River in Beverly rose out of its 29 foot flood stage during the early evening hours of February 25th. The river crested at 29.8 feet a few hours later and returned to its banks just after midnight on the 26th. Fields and farmlands residing adjacent to the river observed minor flooding while the Muskingum River was out of its banks.
